title: Error Correction Of A Logical Qubit Encoded In A Single Atomic Ion
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 13 July 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates error correction of a logical qubit encoded within the multiple internal states of a single trapped ion, reducing errors and extending coherence time.
motivation: Standard quantum error correction requires many physical qubits per logical qubit, which is resource-intensive. Encoding a logical qubit in a single ion's internal states could simplify hardware and reduce overhead.
method: The authors encode a logical qubit in the hyperfine and Zeeman sublevels of a single trapped ion, implement error correction via microwave and laser pulses, and measure error rates and coherence times.
result: The error correction protocol reduces the logical error rate and extends the coherence time compared to the uncorrected physical qubit.
conclusion: Encoding a logical qubit in a single ion is a viable approach to quantum error correction, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Adiabatic Preparation Of Thermal States And Entropy-noise Relation On Noisy Quantum Computers
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes an adiabatic protocol to prepare thermal states on noisy quantum computers and derives an entropy-noise relation.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but current methods are limited by noise and hardware constraints.
method: The authors design an adiabatic state preparation protocol that leverages the system's natural noise to drive the system to a thermal state, and they analyze the entropy production as a function of noise parameters.
result: They demonstrate that the protocol can prepare thermal states with high fidelity on current noisy quantum devices, and they establish a quantitative relation between entropy production and noise strength.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for thermal state preparation and deepens the understanding of entropy production in open quantum systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and quantum simulation.

title: A Resource- And Computationally-efficient Protocol For Multipartite Entanglement Distribution In Bell-pair Networks
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 08 July 2026;

motivation: Efficient distribution of multipartite entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but existing protocols are resource-intensive or computationally complex.
method: The protocol uses a novel combination of entanglement swapping and local operations to generate multipartite states from Bell pairs with reduced resource overhead.
result: The protocol achieves lower qubit and gate counts compared to previous methods, while maintaining high fidelity.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach for multipartite entanglement distribution, advancing quantum network capabilities.

abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;

title: Hybrid Nanophotonic Trap For Cold Atoms Using Surface Forces And A Blue-detuned Evanescent Field
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 09 July 2026;
tldr: A hybrid nanophotonic trap for cold atoms using surface forces and blue-detuned evanescent fields achieves efficient loading and enhanced storage and coherence times.
motivation: To improve the performance of atom-based quantum technologies by developing a robust and efficient trap for cold atoms near nanophotonic structures.
method: The trap combines attractive surface forces (Casimir-Polder) with repulsive blue-detuned evanescent fields to create a stable trapping potential for caesium atoms near a nanophotonic waveguide.
result: The hybrid trap demonstrates efficient loading, long storage times, and long coherence times, outperforming previous approaches.
conclusion: This hybrid trapping scheme is promising for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems, enabling strong atom-light interactions with low loss.

title: Variational Gibbs State Preparation On Trapped-ion Devices
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 11 July 2026;

motivation: Gibbs state preparation is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are resource-intensive; a variational approach offers a more efficient alternative.
method: The authors design a variational ansatz tailored to trapped-ion hardware, optimize it using a classical optimizer, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate successful preparation of Gibbs states for small systems with high fidelity, showing the method's feasibility on current hardware.
conclusion: Variational Gibbs state preparation is a promising route for near-term quantum devices, enabling studies of thermal states and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Classical Simulation With Noisy Quantum Devices
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;

conclusion: Noisy quantum devices can be valuable resources for classical simulation, offering a practical path to extend the reach of classical simulators in the near term.

conclusion: The work provides a unified framework connecting measurement-induced phases, quantum state designs, and entanglement transitions in monitored systems.
